description: Instead of combining scores into a single objective, maintain a Pareto front over multiple stability-related objectives: thermostability (ddG), kinetic stability, aggregation propensity, and expression level. Use multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (NSGA-II) to evolve mutation sets that are Pareto-optimal.
mathematical_formalization: Objectives: f_1(S) = predicted ddG, f_2(S) = recovery probability, f_3(S) = aggregation score, f_4(S) = expression level. S dominates T iff f_i(S) >= f_i(T) for all i and f_j(S) > f_j(T) for some j. NSGA-II with crowding distance for Pareto front diversity.
analogical_connections: Wu et al. (2026): multi-objective optimization achieving +8C Tm with >95% activity retention
LAffAb: co-optimizing antibody affinity and stability with combinatorial libraries
Portfolio optimization: maximizing return while minimizing risk
implementation_hypothesis: Population of 100 mutation sets. Initialize from top single mutants. Crossover: uniform. Mutation: swap one amino acid. NSGA-II selection. 50 generations. Total: 100*50*4 = 20K evaluations.
experiment_seed: Select 10 well-characterized FireProtDB proteins. Run NSGA-II targeting ddG + expression. Compare Pareto front vs single-objective greedy.
